The repository is an STM32CubeMX-generated STM32H7 project (CubeSat1U) using the STM32 HAL and FreeRTOS.

Key facts for an AI coding agent (be directly actionable):

- Project layout to reference
  - `Makefile` — canonical build; outputs live in `build/` (elf/hex/bin and object lists).
  - `CubeSat1U.ioc` — CubeMX project file. Regenerating this will overwrite generated files; user code must stay inside USER CODE BEGIN/END blocks.
  - `Core/Inc`, `Core/Src` — main application code and HAL glue (SystemClock_Config, MX_* init functions).
  - `Core/Lib` — hand-written libraries (e.g. `OV2640.c`, `mpu6050.c`) — preferred place for added drivers.
  - `Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver` and `Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS` — vendor and middleware sources; avoid changing unless necessary.

- Build & toolchain (concrete)
  - Build with GNU ARM toolchain: simply run `make`. The Makefile expects `arm-none-eabi-` tools on PATH or you can pass `GCC_PATH` to `make` (for example on Windows: `make GCC_PATH="C:/path/to/gcc-arm/bin"`).
  - Output binaries: `build/CubeSat1U.elf`, `build/CubeSat1U.hex`, `build/CubeSat1U.bin`.
  - The Makefile is generated by CubeMX; keep changes minimal and prefer editing `CubeSat1U.ioc` when adding/removing peripherals.

- Coding conventions & generated-code constraints
  - CubeMX-generated files use `/* USER CODE BEGIN X */ ... /* USER CODE END X */` markers. Preserve user content inside these blocks; CubeMX may overwrite other regions.
  - HAL drivers are used everywhere (GPIO, I2C, DCMI, UART). Prefer HAL API patterns visible in `Core/Src/main.c` for initialization and callback wiring.
  - FreeRTOS is integrated via CMSIS-RTOS V2 wrappers (look at `Core/Src/freertos.c` / `main.c` thread creation). Use osThreadNew and osDelay as examples.

- Camera (OV2640) integration (exact example to copy)
  - Driver: `Core/Lib/OV2640.c` — uses HAL I2C for control and HAL DCMI + DMA for image capture. Important functions:
    - `OV2640_Init`, `OV2640_Ping`, `OV2640_Reset`, `OV2640_WriteReg/ReadReg`, `OV2640_StartSnapshot`, `OV2640_WaitFrame`, `OV2640_OnFrameEvent`.
    - Example callback to set frame ready: implement `HAL_DCMI_FrameEventCallback()` in user code and call `OV2640_OnFrameEvent(&g_cam);`.
  - Register tables are embedded arrays (e.g. `OV2640_QVGA_RGB565[]`). Replace with the correct register table for real usage.

- Debugging, tests and iteration notes (repo-discoverable)
  - There are no unit tests in the tree. Quick verification: build (`make`) and inspect `build/*.lst` and `build/*.map` artifacts for symbol/section layout (Makefile already produces map and listings).
  - Flashing is not scripted in the Makefile; after building use your normal flashing tool (ST-Link, OpenOCD, STM32CubeProgrammer) to write `build/CubeSat1U.bin` or `build/CubeSat1U.hex`.

- Integration and cross-component patterns
  - Peripherals are configured in CubeMX and initialized in `MX_*` functions in `Core/Src/main.c`. Higher-level modules (drivers in `Core/Lib`) receive HAL handle pointers (e.g. `I2C_HandleTypeDef *hi2c`) — follow that pattern.
  - Shared state uses global handles declared in `Core/Inc/main.h` and defined in `Core/Src/main.c` (e.g., `UART_HandleTypeDef huart2;`). Prefer passing handles into libraries rather than re-declaring globals.

If anything here is unclear or you want this expanded (examples for flashing/backporting to an IDE, more driver usage snippets, or CI-friendly build rules), tell me which section to expand and I will iterate.
